q2_gaps: direct quotation — "said that \"<verbatim quoted clause>\"" is treated as an ordinary that-complement; the instruction set has no rule for preserving quoted wording or distinguishing direct from indirect report

whether a nationality/origin adjective modifier of a fused compound is exposed is underdetermined: the fusion list names nationality (breton_tapestry) but the exposure rule's iff-test ("an adjectival property of the referent", predication test) enumerates only gradable, positional/cardinal and material adjectives, so it is unclear whether (Inheritance british_officer british) is required

an indefinite bare-plural argument ("allegations") inside an episodic clause — the determiner rule sends a bare plural to the generic kind, while the group-witness route used here is specified for definite/counted plurals
notes: Non-factive `say` sealed under Theme with nothing flattened, agentless passives, present-perfect to coarse Past with no spurious Before, past progressive as Past+Ongoing, the multi-word name plus its separate kind atom, and Iraq's Name projected outside the seal are all correct. Into/Against are surface-preposition obliques and are licensed.
